definition_zh: 压碎；压坏；击溃；拥挤的人群
definition_en: to press something so hard that it breaks, or to defeat, or a crowd pressed tight
core_image: 一只脚踩在空罐上，罐身瞬间塌下去
scene: 他抬脚把空罐踩扁，铁皮发出脆响。The machine will crush the stones into fine sand.
sceneCN: 这里 crush 指「压碎」（第 1 个义项：用大力把东西压破压扁）；句意是机器会把石头压成细沙。

senses.title: Press until it breaks
senses.definition: to press something hard until it breaks or loses shape
senses.definitionCN: 用力压某物直到破裂或变形
senses.example: She crushed the garlic with the flat of a knife.
senses.exampleCN: 她用刀面把蒜压碎。
senses.why: Weight plus a hard surface ends a shape.
senses.whyCN: 重量加上硬面，就终结了一个形状。

senses.title: Defeat completely
senses.definition: to beat an opponent completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底打败对手
senses.example: The home team crushed the visitors by five goals.
senses.exampleCN: 主队以五球大胜客队。
senses.why: What is pressed flat cannot stand up again.
senses.whyCN: 被压平的东西，站不起来了。

senses.title: A tight crowd
senses.definition: a crowd pressed so tightly that movement is hard
senses.definitionCN: 挤得难以移动的人群
senses.example: We were caught in a crush at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 我们被堵在门口的拥挤人群里。
senses.why: Bodies packed like seeds in one pod.
senses.whyCN: 身体挤在一起，像豆荚里的豆子。

intro.en: Crush comes from Old French cruissir, to crack or gnash, perhaps from a Frankish word for pressing.
intro.cn: crush 源自古法语 cruissir（使裂开、咬牙），可能出自表示挤压的法兰克语词。

items.en: Cruissir meant to crack or to gnash the teeth.
items.cn: cruissir 意为使裂开或咬牙。

items.en: Crush first meant to break something by pressing.
items.cn: crush 最初指用挤压把东西弄破。

items.en: It was used for armies that broke an enemy.
items.cn: 它被用于形容军队击溃敌人。

items.en: A crowd pressed tight was called a crush.
items.cn: 挤得紧紧的人群被称为 crush。

items.en: It also names a strong but passing liking.
items.cn: 它也表示一种强烈却短暂的喜欢。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cr- opening and a hissing end, and the meaning group names other kinds of pressing and breaking.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cr- 开头与嘶声结尾，近义组列出其他挤压与破坏的说法。

entries.definition: the hard outer layer of bread
a tool with stiff hairs
a loud fall or collision
to press something flat
to break into pieces with force
to beat someone in a contest

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a can under a foot and end with a team that cannot stand up.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只被踩在脚下的罐子开始，落到一支站不起来的队伍。

normal.en: A foot and a can explain the whole word.
normal.cn: 一只脚和一只罐子，就解释了整个词。

normal.en: Press until the shape gives up.
normal.cn: 一直压，直到形状认输。

normal.en: A crushed team leaves the field flat.
normal.cn: 被击溃的队伍像被压平一样离场。

normal.en: In a crush, elbows do the talking.
normal.cn: 在拥挤的人群里，胳膊肘在说话。

normal.en: A crush is a feeling pressed into a small space.
normal.cn: 迷恋是被压进小小空间里的一份感情。

abstract.en: Picture a can folding under a boot.
abstract.cn: 想象一只罐子在靴子下折下去。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd so tight that no one can turn.
abstract.cn: 想象人群紧得谁也没法转身。

abstract.en: Picture a paper cup flattened on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一只纸杯被压扁在桌上。

examples.en: Do not crush the box; it holds glass.
examples.cn: 别把箱子压坏，里面有玻璃。

examples.en: The team crushed its rival in the final.
examples.cn: 这支队伍在决赛中击溃了对手。

examples.en: She was caught in the crush at the door.
examples.cn: 她被堵在门口的拥挤人群里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crush 记成「压到出声」：cr 像裂开的声响，ush 像一口气被挤出来。

root: 源自古法语 cruissir（使裂开、咬牙），可能出自表示挤压的法兰克语词；本义是压到破裂，后引申为击溃与挤紧的人群。

sensesIntro.en: From pressing a thing until it breaks, to breaking an enemy, to a crowd pressed tight.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把东西压破，到击溃对手，再到挤紧的人群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boot coming down on an empty can.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只靴子踩在一只空罐上。

branches.en: Pressing hard enough ends the shape of a thing.
branches.cn: 压得够狠，东西的形状就没了。

branches.en: A beaten team is a shape pressed flat.
branches.cn: 被打败的队伍，就是被压平的形状。

branches.en: A crowd can press bodies as a hand presses a can.
branches.cn: 人群挤身体，就像手挤罐子。

branches.en: The same force breaks metal and breaks a rival.
branches.cn: 同一种力既弄坏金属，也弄垮对手。

branches.en: Defeat and crowding both leave no room to move.
branches.cn: 失败与拥挤都让人没有转身的空间。

intro.en: Crush gathers words for pressing, breaking, and the machines that do it.
intro.cn: crush 这一族词围绕压、破，以及做这些事的机器。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the word comes from Old French cruissir, to crack.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根；这个词来自古法语 cruissir（使裂开）。

items.example: The news was a crushing blow.
items.exampleCN: 这消息是毁灭性的打击。

items.example: The box is crushable and light.

items.exampleCN: 他直白得让人招架不住。

items.meaning: a fence that holds back a crowd
items.example: Police stood at the crush barrier.
The worker had a crush injury.

definition_en: the hard outer layer of bread, or any hard covering on a surface
core_image: 一只刚出炉的面包，表皮被敲出脆响
scene: 面包刚出炉，手指一弹表皮就发出脆响。A thick crust keeps the loaf soft inside.
sceneCN: 这里 crust 指「面包皮」（第 1 个义项：面包外面烤硬的一层）；句意是厚厚的外皮让面包里面保持柔软。

senses.title: The outer bread layer
senses.definition: the hard baked outer layer of bread
senses.definitionCN: 面包烤硬的外层
senses.example: She cut the crust off her sandwich.
senses.exampleCN: 她把三明治的边切掉了。
senses.why: Heat dries the outside first, sealing the soft inside.
senses.whyCN: 热先烤干外面，把柔软封在里面。

senses.title: A hard outer shell
senses.definition: a hard layer that forms on the outside of something
senses.definitionCN: 在某物外面形成的一层硬壳
senses.example: A crust of ice covered the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 一层冰盖住了池塘。
senses.why: Cold air hardens the surface it touches.
senses.whyCN: 冷空气把它碰到的表面变硬。

senses.title: The outer shell of the earth
senses.definition: the solid outer layer of the earth
senses.definitionCN: 地球坚硬的外层
senses.example: Earthquakes start deep in the crust.
senses.exampleCN: 地震始于地壳深处。
senses.why: Even a planet wears a baked skin.
senses.whyCN: 连一颗行星也披着一层烤硬的外皮。

intro.en: Crust comes from Latin crusta, a rind or hard shell, through Old French crouste.
intro.cn: crust 源自拉丁语 crusta（外壳、硬皮），经古法语 crouste 进入英语。

items.en: Crusta meant a rind or a hard outer shell.
items.cn: crusta 指外皮或坚硬的壳。

items.en: It covered bread, cheese, and the face of stone.
items.cn: 它可用于面包、奶酪与石头表面。

items.en: Crouste named the baked outside of bread.
items.cn: crouste 指面包烤硬的外层。

items.en: Crust meant the hard outside of a loaf.
items.cn: crust 指面包硬的外层。

items.en: It extended to the hard outer layer of the earth.
items.cn: 它扩展到地球坚硬的表层。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cr- opening and a hard final sound, and the meaning group names other outer coverings.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cr- 开头与硬收尾，近义组列出其他外层的说法。

entries.definition: to press until something breaks
a very small piece of bread
the red coat on old iron
the thick outer skin of fruit
a hard case around something
a layer spread over a surface

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a warm loaf and end with the skin of a planet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只热面包开始，落到一颗行星的外皮。

normal.en: Break the crust and steam comes out.
normal.cn: 掰开外皮，热气就冒出来。

normal.en: The crust is the part that took the heat.
normal.cn: 外皮是承受了热的那一层。

normal.en: Bread, ice, and the earth all wear one.
normal.cn: 面包、冰和大地都披着一层。

normal.en: A crusty loaf is loud when you press it.
normal.cn: 硬皮面包一按就响。

normal.en: Under the crust, everything stays soft.
normal.cn: 外皮之下，一切都还柔软。

abstract.en: Picture a knife tapping a loaf and hearing a knock.
abstract.cn: 想象刀背敲在面包上，听见一声脆响。

abstract.en: Picture thin ice holding a stone on a pond.
abstract.cn: 想象薄冰托着池塘上的一块石头。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line between soil and deep rock.
abstract.cn: 想象泥土与深岩之间的一条细线。

examples.en: The pie has a golden crust.
examples.cn: 这个馅饼有一层金黄的皮。

examples.en: Salt crusted the roads after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后路面结了一层盐壳。

examples.en: The crust of the earth is thin under the ocean.
examples.cn: 海洋下方的地壳很薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crust 记成「烤硬的一层」：面包、冰面、地壳，都是外面先硬的那层。

root: 源自拉丁语 crusta（外壳、硬皮），经古法语 crouste 进入英语；本义是面包外层烤硬的部分，后扩展为任何硬层与地壳。

sensesIntro.en: From the baked outside of bread, to any hard layer, to the shell of the earth.
sensesIntro.cn: 从面包烤硬的外层，到任何硬层，再到地球的外壳。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm loaf with a crisp brown shell.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带着焦脆棕色外壳的热面包。

branches.en: The oven hardens the outside of the bread.
branches.cn: 炉火把面包的外层烤硬。

branches.en: Cold or salt can build a hard layer too.
branches.cn: 寒冷或盐也能结出一层硬壳。

branches.en: The whole planet rests inside one thin shell.
branches.cn: 整颗行星都包在一层薄壳里。

branches.en: Bread and ice both dry into a shell.
branches.cn: 面包与冰都干成一层壳。

branches.en: The same word covers a pond and a planet.
branches.cn: 同一个词既盖住池塘，也盖住行星。

intro.en: Crust brings a small family of words for hard outer layers and the things that wear them.
intro.cn: crust 带来一小族词，都与坚硬的外层以及披着外层的物有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crusta, a rind, is the root behind crust and crustacean.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crusta（外皮）是 crust 与 crustacean 背后的根。

items.example: The bread has a dark crust.
items.exampleCN: 这面包有一层深色外皮。

items.example: The boots were crusted with mud.
She asked for a crustless sandwich.
items.exampleCN: 她要了一份去边的三明治。

items.meaning: to cover with a hard layer
to form a hard top layer
items.example: The snow crusted over at night.
items.exampleCN: 夜里雪面结了一层硬壳。

definition_zh: 甲壳动物（虾、蟹、藤壶等有硬壳的节肢动物）
definition_en: an arthropod with a hard shell, such as a crab, shrimp, lobster or barnacle
core_image: 潮池石缝里一只螃蟹举起硬壳钳子，壳面反着水光
scene: 潮池里，一只小蟹横着快跑，硬壳在浅水中反着光。 A small crustacean scuttled sideways through the pool, its hard shell glinting under the water.
sceneCN: 这里 crustacean 指「甲壳动物」（第 1 个义项：有硬壳的节肢动物）；句意为一只小甲壳动物横着穿过潮池，硬壳在水下反光。

derivatives.zh: 十足目动物（蟹、虾等甲壳动物）

senses.title: A member of the group Crustacea
senses.definition: any arthropod of the group Crustacea, with a hard exoskeleton and usually two pairs of antennae
senses.definitionCN: 甲壳动物类群中任何有硬外骨骼、通常有两对触角的节肢动物
senses.example: A small crustacean scuttled sideways through the pool.
senses.exampleCN: 一只小甲壳动物横着穿过潮池。
senses.why: The name comes from Latin crusta 'shell', because the group is defined by its hard casing.
senses.whyCN: 名字来自拉丁 crusta「硬壳」，因为这一类群正是以硬壳为标志。

senses.title: The group as a whole
senses.definition: the crustaceans collectively, treated as one large subgroup of arthropods
senses.definitionCN: 把所有甲壳动物作为一个大的节肢动物亚群来看
senses.example: Crustaceans dominate the tide pool at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里潮池由甲壳类占据主导。
senses.why: Collective use lets the plural stand for the group without naming each species.
senses.whyCN: 集合用法让复数形式代表整个类群，无需逐一命名物种。

senses.title: An edible crustacean
senses.definition: a crab, shrimp, lobster or similar animal harvested for food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物捕捞的蟹、虾、龙虾或类似动物
senses.example: The restaurant buys crustaceans from the local boats.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅从本地渔船购买甲壳类。
senses.why: Fisheries use the group name for the catch, so it doubles as a menu category.
senses.whyCN: 渔业用类群名指渔获，因此它同时成了菜单类别。

senses.title: The hard shell itself
senses.definition: the chitinous exoskeleton that a crustacean sheds as it grows
senses.definitionCN: 甲壳动物生长时蜕去的几丁质外骨骼
senses.example: The crustacean shell left behind was perfectly intact.
senses.exampleCN: 留下的甲壳完好无损。
senses.why: The shell is shed whole, so the word can name the casing apart from the animal.
senses.whyCN: 壳是整片蜕下的，因此这个词也能指脱离动物体的外壳。

senses.title: A fossil crustacean
senses.definition: ancient crustacean remains, common as microfossils in marine rocks
senses.definitionCN: 古代甲壳动物的遗骸，常以微体化石形式存在于海相岩石中
senses.example: Ostracods are tiny crustaceans used to date the core.
senses.exampleCN: 介形虫是微小的甲壳动物，用来给岩芯定年。
senses.why: Their shed shells fossilize well, which makes the group a geological tool.
senses.whyCN: 它们蜕下的壳容易形成化石，使这一类群成了地质工具。

senses.title: A parasitic crustacean
senses.definition: a crustacean that lives on or in another animal, such as a sea louse on a fish
senses.definitionCN: 附着在另一动物体表或体内生活的甲壳动物，如鱼身上的海虱
senses.example: Sea lice are crustaceans that damage farmed salmon.
senses.exampleCN: 海虱是危害养殖鲑鱼的甲壳动物。
senses.why: Parasitism evolved repeatedly in the group, so the word covers very different life habits.
senses.whyCN: 寄生在类群内多次演化出现，因此这个词涵盖差异极大的生活方式。

senses.title: A laboratory model
senses.definition: a crustacean used in research, such as Daphnia in toxicity tests
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究的甲壳动物，如毒性测试中的水蚤
senses.example: Daphnia is a crustacean used in standard toxicity tests.
senses.exampleCN: 水蚤是标准毒性测试中使用的一种甲壳动物。
senses.why: Short life cycles and sensitivity to chemicals make some crustaceans ideal test animals.
senses.whyCN: 生活史短、对化学品敏感，使某些甲壳动物成为理想的试验动物。

senses.title: A farmed crop
senses.definition: a crustacean raised in ponds or tanks for food
senses.definitionCN: 在池塘或水箱中为食用而养殖的甲壳动物
senses.example: Shrimp are the most valuable crustaceans in aquaculture.
senses.exampleCN: 虾是水产养殖中价值最高的甲壳类。
senses.why: Farming turns the animal into a commodity, and the group name becomes an industry label.
senses.whyCN: 养殖把动物变成商品，类群名也成了行业标签。

intro.en: Crustacean is built on Latin crusta 'crust, shell' plus the adjective ending -aceus, and entered English through scientific Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: crustacean 由拉丁 crusta「硬壳、外壳」加形容词词尾 -aceus 构成，经科学拉丁语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Crusta meant 'crust, rind, shell', the hard outer layer of bread or of an animal. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: crusta 意为「硬壳、外皮、外壳」，指面包或动物体表的硬层。其更深来源未有定论。

items.en: The adjective crustaceus 'having a crust or shell' was used for animals with hard coverings, not only for crabs.
items.cn: 形容词 crustaceus「有壳的」用于带硬覆盖的动物，并不只指蟹。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century zoology raised Crustacea to a formal group name, separating crabs, shrimp and barnacles from insects.
items.cn: 18、19 世纪动物学把 Crustacea 提升为正式类群名，把蟹、虾、藤壶与昆虫分开。

items.en: English crustacean appears in the nineteenth century as the noun for a member of that group, alongside the older adjective crustaceous.
items.cn: 英语 crustacean 在 19 世纪作为该类群成员的名称出现，与更早的形容词 crustaceous 并存。

items.en: As seafood industries grew, crustacean became the neutral word for crabs and shrimp on menus and in regulations.
items.cn: 随着海产行业发展，crustacean 成了菜单与法规中对蟹、虾的中性称谓。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): crusta has no agreed etymology, so any pre-Latin form proposed for it is a reconstruction, not a documented word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：crusta 没有公认词源，凡为其提出的拉丁语之前形式都属重构，而非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds crust- words that look close but name shells, rocks or a geological period; group two holds animal-group words easily confused with crustacean.
note.cn: 第一组是同含 crust- 但指外壳、地壳或地质年代的形近词；第二组是易与甲壳动物混淆的动物类群词。

entries.definition: The hard outer layer of bread or rock; it is the source noun, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 面包或岩石的硬外层；它是来源名词，不是动物。

entries.definition: Meaning 'having a crust'; it describes the shell but does not name a crab or shrimp.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「有硬壳的」；它描述外壳，却不指蟹或虾。

entries.definition: Relating to the crust of the Earth; the same noun, an entirely different field.
entries.definitionCN: 与地壳有关的；同出一个名词，却属完全不同的领域。

entries.definition: The geological period named from Latin creta 'chalk', not crusta; the similar ending is a false friend.
entries.definitionCN: 地质年代名，来自拉丁 creta「白垩」，而非 crusta；词尾相似是假朋友。

entries.definition: Any jointed-legged invertebrate with an exoskeleton; crustaceans are one branch of the arthropods.
entries.definitionCN: 任何有外骨骼、具分节附肢的无脊椎动物；甲壳动物是节肢动物的一个分支。

entries.definition: A market term for edible crustaceans and mollusks together, broader and looser than crustacean.
entries.definitionCN: 市场用语，兼指可食甲壳动物与软体动物，比 crustacean 更宽泛、更松散。

entries.definition: A crustacean with ten legs, such as a crab or lobster; it is a subgroup, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 有十条腿的甲壳动物，如蟹或龙虾；它是亚群，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A crustacean that cements itself to rocks or hulls; it is a crustacean even though it looks like a shell.
entries.definitionCN: 把自己黏在岩石或船体上的甲壳动物；虽像贝壳，它仍是甲壳动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: crust- means 'shell': a crustacean is the shelled animal.
normal.cn: crust- 意为「壳」：甲壳动物就是带壳的动物。

normal.en: Crabs, shrimp, lobsters and barnacles are all crustaceans, though they look very different.
normal.cn: 蟹、虾、龙虾、藤壶都是甲壳动物，尽管外形差异很大。

normal.en: A crustacean is an arthropod, but not every arthropod is a crustacean: insects and spiders are outside the group.
normal.cn: 甲壳动物是节肢动物，但并非所有节肢动物都是甲壳动物：昆虫与蜘蛛不在其中。

normal.en: Shellfish is the menu word; crustacean is the biological one.
normal.cn: shellfish 是菜单用语；crustacean 是生物学用语。

normal.en: Decapods are the ten-legged crustaceans, the ones most often eaten.
normal.cn: 十足目是有十条腿的甲壳动物，也是最常被食用的一类。

abstract.en: Picture an animal wearing its skeleton on the outside and shedding it to grow.
abstract.cn: 想象一个把骨骼穿在外面的动物，靠蜕掉它来长大。

abstract.en: Picture a barnacle that looks like a shell but is actually a shrimp glued down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只藤壶，看起来像贝壳，其实是一只黏住的虾。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a shelled animal through its roles: group member, collective group, seafood, shed shell, fossil, parasite, lab model and farmed crop.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个带壳动物穿过各种角色：类群成员、整体类群、海产食物、蜕下的壳、化石、寄生虫、实验模型与养殖对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crab in a tide pool, its hard shell reflecting the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：潮池里的一只蟹，硬壳映着水光。

branches.en: ONE AND MANY: a single shelled animal, or the whole group treated as a unit.
branches.cn: 个体与整体：单个带壳动物，或把整个类群当作一个单位。

branches.en: COMMODITY: the same animal appears on a menu and in a farm pond.
branches.cn: 商品：同一种动物既出现在菜单上，也出现在养殖池里。

branches.en: THE CAST-OFF: the shell can be named apart from the living animal.
branches.cn: 蜕下之物：壳可以脱离活体单独被指称。

branches.en: EVIDENCE AND EXPERIMENT: shed shells become fossils; small species become test subjects.
branches.cn: 证据与实验：蜕壳变成化石；小型种类成为试验对象。

branches.en: THE OTHER LIFESTYLE: some crustaceans live on other animals.
branches.cn: 另一种活法：有些甲壳动物寄居在其他动物身上。

intro.en: Crustacean is a Latin-derived noun plus the English suffix -an; the stem is the same one that gives crust and crustal.

latinIntro.en: Latin crusta gives crust, crustaceus and crustulum; crustaceus plus the group name Crustacea produced the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crusta 衍生 crust、crustaceus 与 crustulum；crustaceus 加类群名 Crustacea 产生了英语名词。

items.example: The root supplies the shell image.

senses.title: Of hidden meaning

senses.why: A door behind a painting.
senses.whyCN: 画后的门。

senses.title: Brief and puzzling

senses.definitionCN: 短得让人只能猜

senses.exampleCN: 他莫测地一点头。
senses.why: A half-open eye.

items.en: Kryptos meant hidden.
items.cn: kryptos 意为隐藏的。

items.en: Kryptikos meant fitted for hiding.

items.en: Crypticus kept the hidden sense.

items.en: Cryptic meant secret or occult.

items.en: Cryptic named puzzling clues and remarks.

normal.en: A crypt is an underground room.

normal.en: Cryptic things are hidden like a crypt.
normal.cn: 隐晦的东西像地窖一样藏着。

normal.en: A cryptic note hides its point.

normal.en: A cryptic smile says nothing clear.

normal.en: Cryptic clues need decoding.

definition_en: a clear mineral, or a solid whose parts form a regular repeating shape
core_image: 一块透明的水晶，棱面把光折成几道
scene: 窗台上有一块透明的水晶，阳光穿过去散成几道光。The crystal caught the light and threw small rainbows on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 crystal 指「水晶」（第 1 个义项：透明且带规则棱面的矿物）；句意是水晶接住光，在墙上投出小小的彩虹。

senses.title: Clear mineral
senses.definition: a clear hard mineral used in jewellery and glass
senses.definitionCN: 用于首饰与玻璃的透明坚硬矿物
senses.example: The ring holds a small crystal.
senses.exampleCN: 戒指上镶着一小块水晶。
senses.why: Light passes through it without being swallowed.
senses.whyCN: 光穿过它，没有被吞掉。

senses.title: A regular solid form
senses.definition: a solid whose particles form a regular repeating shape
senses.definitionCN: 微粒排成规则重复形状的固体
senses.example: Salt forms small crystals as it dries.
senses.exampleCN: 盐在变干时结成小晶体。
senses.why: Order appears when a liquid lets go of heat.
senses.whyCN: 液体放下热，秩序就出现了。

senses.title: Fine glassware

senses.definitionCN: 高质量玻璃或用水晶制成的器物

senses.why: Purity of material shows in how it rings.
senses.whyCN: 材料纯不纯，听它敲响就知道。

intro.en: Crystal comes from Greek krystallos, ice, through Latin crystallum and Old French cristal.
intro.cn: crystal 源自希腊语 krystallos（冰），经拉丁语 crystallum 与古法语 cristal 进入英语。

items.en: Krystallos meant ice.
items.cn: krystallos 意为冰。

items.en: It was used for clear rock that looked like frozen water.
items.cn: 它被用来指像冻住的水一样的透明石头。

items.en: Crystallum kept both the ice and the clear stone senses.
items.cn: crystallum 同时保留冰与透明石头两层意思。

items.en: Cristal named clear stone and fine glass.
items.cn: cristal 指透明石头与精细玻璃。

items.en: Crystal meant a clear mineral with flat faces.
items.cn: crystal 指带平面棱的透明矿物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crystall- stem or the cr- opening, and the meaning group names other clear solids.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crystall- 词干或 cr- 开头，近义组列出其他透明固体的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with frozen water that never melts and end with a glass that sings.

normal.en: The Greeks called clear stone ice, and the name stuck.
normal.cn: 希腊人把透明石头叫作冰，这名字就留下了。

normal.en: Light goes in white and comes out in colors.
normal.cn: 光白白地进去，出来时带了颜色。

normal.en: Salt and sugar build the same shape, smaller.
normal.cn: 盐和糖也会长出同样的形状，只是更小。

normal.en: Tap a crystal glass and hear how pure it is.
normal.cn: 敲一下水晶杯，就听得出它有多纯。

normal.en: A crystal is order you can hold in your hand.
normal.cn: 水晶是能握在手里的秩序。

abstract.en: Picture a stone with edges sharp as cut glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一块棱边像切玻璃一样锋利的石头。

abstract.en: Picture a thin rainbow lying on a white wall.
abstract.cn: 想象白墙上一道细细的彩虹。

abstract.en: Picture a snowflake that kept its shape all year.
abstract.cn: 想象一片整年都没化掉的雪花。

examples.en: The cave is full of tall crystal columns.
examples.cn: 洞穴里满是高大的水晶柱。

examples.en: These crystals grow slowly in cold water.
examples.cn: 这些晶体在冷水里慢慢长成。

examples.en: She poured the juice into a crystal glass.
examples.cn: 她把果汁倒进一只水晶杯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crystal 记成「冻住的光」：希腊人叫它冰（krystallos），透明石头就像冻住的水。

root: 源自希腊语 krystallos（冰），经拉丁语 crystallum 与古法语 cristal 进入英语；本义是像冻住的水一样透明的石头，后指水晶、结晶与水晶玻璃。

sensesIntro.en: From a clear mineral, to a regular solid form, to fine glass that rings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从透明矿物，到规则的固体形态，再到敲之有声的精细玻璃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear stone splitting sunlight into colors.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块透明石头把阳光分成几种颜色。

branches.en: The stone is valued because light can cross it.
branches.cn: 这块石头珍贵，是因为光能穿过它。

branches.en: Small particles line up and repeat the same shape.
branches.cn: 小颗粒排好队，一遍遍重复同一形状。

branches.en: Fine glass carries the same name in a cup.
branches.cn: 精细玻璃做成杯子，也叫这个名字。

branches.en: The big stone and the small grain share one order.
branches.cn: 大石头与小颗粒共享同一种秩序。

branches.en: Clear stone and clear glass both let light speak.
branches.cn: 透明石头与透明玻璃都让光说话。

intro.en: Crystal grows a family of words for clear stone, regular shapes, and the act of forming them.

latinIntro.en: The Greek krystallos, ice, is the root under crystal and crystalline.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 krystallos（冰）是 crystal 与 crystalline 背后的根。

definition_zh: 结晶；使结晶；（想法、计划）变得明确；裹糖（糖渍）
definition_en: to form crystals or cause something to form crystals; to become or make something clear and definite
core_image: 作坊里，裹了糖的姜片摊在竹筛上晾干，糖层慢慢结成白色颗粒
scene: 作坊里，师傅把煮好的姜片裹上糖，摊在竹筛上晾干，糖层慢慢结成白色颗粒。The ginger slices crystallize as the sugar syrup cools around them.
sceneCN: 这里 crystallize 指「（糖浆在表面）结晶、形成糖霜」（第 5 个义项：用糖包裹并使其结晶，即糖渍）；句意为糖浆在姜片周围冷却时，姜片逐渐结晶挂霜。可辨识物件：竹筛、糖渍姜片、白色糖霜、冷却的糖浆。

senses.title: Form crystals (intransitive)
senses.definition: of a substance: to separate from a liquid as ordered solid crystals
senses.definitionCN: 指物质从液体中析出为有序固体晶体
senses.example: The ginger slices crystallize as the sugar syrup cools around them.
senses.exampleCN: 糖浆在姜片周围冷却时，姜片逐渐结晶挂霜。
senses.why: The intransitive use describes the substance acting on its own.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法描述物质自身发生的变化。

senses.title: Cause crystals to form
senses.definition: to make a dissolved substance form crystals, as by cooling or seeding
senses.definitionCN: 指通过降温或加晶种使溶解物形成晶体
senses.example: Chemists crystallize the compound by cooling its saturated solution.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家通过冷却饱和溶液使化合物结晶。
senses.why: The transitive use adds an agent who cools or seeds the solution.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法增加一个降温或加晶种的施事。

senses.title: Become definite
senses.definition: of plans or ideas: to take a clear and fixed form after being vague
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或想法从模糊变得清晰固定
senses.example: Their vague proposal crystallized into a detailed scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 他们含糊的提议具体成了一项详细方案。
senses.why: Plans become definite the way crystals become solid.
senses.whyCN: 计划变明确，正如晶体变固体。

senses.title: Make something definite
senses.definition: to give a clear and fixed form to an idea, plan or movement
senses.definitionCN: 指使想法、计划或运动取得清晰固定的形态
senses.example: The speech crystallized the demands of the movement.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇演说把这场运动的要求明确固定下来。
senses.why: An agent can make an idea definite, matching the transitive pattern.
senses.whyCN: 施事可以使想法变明确，与及物模式相合。

senses.title: Coat and preserve with sugar
senses.definition: to coat fruit or peel with sugar syrup that then crystallizes
senses.definitionCN: 指用糖浆包裹水果或果皮，并使糖层结晶
senses.example: They crystallize orange peel for the holiday market.
senses.exampleCN: 他们糖渍橙皮供应节日市场。
senses.why: Sugar coating is literal crystallization on a fruit's surface.
senses.whyCN: 裹糖就是字面意义上的结晶发生在果皮表面。

senses.title: Freeze into ice crystals
senses.definition: of water: to turn into ice crystals, especially in food or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 指水结成冰晶，尤指在食品或组织中
senses.example: Water crystallizes in the cells and bursts them.
senses.exampleCN: 水在细胞里结晶，把细胞胀破。
senses.why: Water in cells crystallizes and expands, which is why it bursts them.
senses.whyCN: 细胞里的水结晶并膨胀，这正是它胀破细胞的原因。

senses.title: Separate out as crystals
senses.definition: to come out of a solution as solid crystals, often with 'out'
senses.definitionCN: 指从溶液中以固体晶体形式析出，常与 out 连用
senses.example: The salt crystallized out as the water evaporated.
senses.exampleCN: 水蒸发时盐结晶析出。
senses.why: The particle out marks separation from solution.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 out 标记从溶液中分离出来。

senses.title: Develop into a clear form
senses.definition: to develop into a recognizable and organized form, often with 'into'
senses.definitionCN: 指发展成可辨识、有组织的形态，常与 into 连用
senses.example: The protest crystallized into a national campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 这场抗议发展成一场全国性运动。
senses.why: The particle into marks development into a recognized form.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 into 标记发展为可辨识的形态。

intro.en: Crystallize is an English verb coined on crystal with the Latin-derived suffix -ize, following the pattern of French and Latin verbs in -iser and -izare.
intro.cn: crystallize 是在 crystal 上加拉丁来源后缀 -ize 构成的英语动词，仿照法语 -iser 与拉丁 -izare 的动词模式。

items.en: Krystallos 'ice, rock crystal' gave Latin crystallus and English crystal.
items.cn: krystallos「冰、水晶」产生拉丁 crystallus 与英语 crystal。

items.en: Latin -izare, from Greek -izein, formed verbs meaning 'to make or become'; it entered English through French -iser.
items.cn: 拉丁 -izare（源自希腊 -izein）构成表示「使……、成为……」的动词，经法语 -iser 进入英语。

items.en: The verb appears in seventeenth-century chemical writing for the formation of salt crystals from solution.
items.cn: 这个动词在十七世纪化学文献中出现，指盐从溶液中形成晶体。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology applied the verb to minerals forming from cooling magma and to ice forming in rock cracks.
items.cn: 十九世纪地质学把这个动词用于矿物从冷却岩浆中形成，以及岩石裂隙中冰的形成。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries crystallize became a common figure for ideas and movements taking definite shape.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，crystallize 成为想法与运动取得明确形态的常用比喻。

items.en: Not uncertain: the formation from crystal plus -ize is transparent. Only the exact first date of the figurative use is approximate.
items.cn: 并非存疑：由 crystal 加 -ize 构成这一点清楚可读。仅比喻义的准确首次年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that look like crystallize but differ in root or spelling; group two holds verbs for becoming solid or definite.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似但词根或拼写不同的动词；第二组是表示变硬或变明确的动词。

entries.definition: The British spelling with -ise; it is the same verb, not a different process.
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写，用 -ise；是同一个动词，不是另一过程。

entries.definition: To burn tissue to stop bleeding, from Greek kautēr 'branding iron'; it shares the ending only.
entries.definitionCN: 指烧灼组织以止血，来自希腊 kautēr「烙铁」；只共享词尾。

entries.definition: The noun from which the verb is formed; it names the object that results, not the action that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 构成该动词的名词；它命名产生的结果对象，而非产生它的动作。

entries.definition: The past participle and adjective, as in crystallized fruit; it names the result, not the action.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词兼形容词，如糖渍水果；它命名结果而非动作。

entries.definition: The general verb for turning liquid into solid; crystallize adds the idea of ordered growth.
entries.definitionCN: 指液体变固体的总称；crystallize 增加有序生长之意。

entries.definition: To come out of a solution as a solid, often without crystal order; a chemical rather than a structural emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 指从溶液中析出固体，常无晶体秩序；强调化学而非结构。

entries.definition: To become hard or firm, without saying anything about internal order.
entries.definitionCN: 指变硬变坚，不涉及内部秩序。

entries.definition: An idiom for a plan or idea becoming definite; crystallize is its more formal single-word equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 指计划或想法变明确的口语说法；crystallize 是更正式的单词对应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real phrasal verbs and the real confectionery use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的短语动词与真实的糖渍用法。

normal.en: Crystal plus -ize: to make or become crystal, exactly as the suffix says.
normal.cn: crystal 加 -ize：使成晶体或成为晶体，正如后缀所示。

normal.en: Two phrasal verbs carry much of the meaning: crystallize out and crystallize into.
normal.cn: 两个短语动词承载了大部分词义：结晶析出与具体形成为。

normal.en: The family runs crystal, crystalline, crystallize, crystallization, crystallized.
normal.cn: 词族包括 crystal、crystalline、crystallize、crystallization、crystallized。

normal.en: In the kitchen the verb means candied: crystallized ginger, crystallized peel.
normal.cn: 在厨房里这个动词指糖渍：糖姜片、糖橙皮。

normal.en: In writing it means making an idea sharp: a speech crystallizes demands.
normal.cn: 在写作中它指使想法锐利：一篇演说把要求明确下来。

abstract.en: Picture a fog that suddenly knows what shape it wants to be.
abstract.cn: 想象一片雾突然知道自己想成为什么形状。

abstract.en: Picture an argument freezing into a single clear sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争论冻结成一句清楚的话。

abstract.en: Picture sugar putting on armour one grain at a time.

examples.en: Salt crystallizes out when the brine is concentrated.
examples.cn: 盐水浓缩时盐结晶析出。

examples.en: The movement crystallized into a political party within a year.
examples.cn: 这场运动在一年内发展成一个政党。

examples.en: Crystallized ginger is sold in small paper bags.
examples.cn: 糖姜片装在小纸袋里出售。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克瑞斯（crystal）来（li）z」——让东西像水晶那样定形 → 结晶、明确

root: crystal（希腊 krystallos「冰、水晶」）+ -ize（拉丁 -izare，源自希腊 -izein，使……、成为……）→ crystallize「使结晶；使明确」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one verb in two directions: matter forms crystals, and ideas form shapes, with sugar, ice, solutions and movements each taking part.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个动词朝两个方向展开：物质结成晶体，想法结成形体，糖、冰、溶液与运动各自参与其中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: syrup drying into a hard white coat on a slice of ginger.
core.cn: 核心意象：糖浆在姜片上晾成一层硬白霜。

branches.en: MAKE AND BECOME: the verb works both without and with an object.
branches.cn: 使然与自然：这个动词既可不及物，也可及物。

branches.en: THE IDEA SETS: vague proposals harden into schemes and demands.
branches.cn: 想法定形：含糊的提议硬化为方案与要求。

branches.en: KITCHEN AND ICE: sugar and water both crystallize on a surface or in a cell.
branches.cn: 厨房与冰：糖与水都会在表面或细胞内结晶。

branches.en: OUT OF SOLUTION: the technical phrasal verb for material leaving a liquid as solid.
branches.cn: 从溶液中析出：物质以固体离开液体的技术短语。

branches.en: INTO A FORM: a movement develops a recognizable body.
branches.cn: 成为形态：一场运动发展出可辨识的躯体。

intro.en: Crystallize is a noun plus a verb-forming suffix, and the suffix is shared with hundreds of English verbs.
intro.cn: crystallize 是名词加动词后缀，这个后缀与数百个英语动词共享。

latinIntro.en: Latin crystallus gives the base; -izare, from Greek -izein, gives the verb pattern seen in organize, realize and crystallize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crystallus 提供词基；-izare（源自希腊 -izein）提供 organize、realize、crystallize 中的动词模式。

items.cn: 它扩展到举止、技能与朋友。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cultiv- stem, and the meaning group names other kinds of careful growth.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cultiv- 词干，近义组列出其他用心培育的说法。

entries.definition: trained and refined in manner
entries.definitionCN: 举止受过训练而文雅的

entries.definition: of the way a people lives
a small group with strong beliefs
to grow crops on land
to care for something as it grows
to grow stronger or fuller over time
entries.definitionCN: 随时间变得更强或更完整

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hand in the soil and end with a friendship kept for years.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从土里的一只手开始，落到维系多年的友谊。

normal.en: Cultivate is care repeated, not a single act.
normal.cn: cultivate 是反复的照料，不是一次性的动作。

normal.en: Turn the soil, drop the seed, wait.
normal.cn: 翻土，下种，然后等。

normal.en: A skill grows like a plant, on small daily water.
normal.cn: 本事像植物，靠每天一点点水长大。

normal.en: You can cultivate beans, a habit, or a friend.
normal.cn: 你可以种豆，也可以培养习惯或结交朋友。

normal.en: Whatever is cultivated stops being wild.
normal.cn: 被栽培过的东西，就不再是野生的。

abstract.en: Picture a hoe turning dark soil in the morning.
abstract.cn: 想象清晨一把锄头翻起黑土。

abstract.en: Picture a green shoot beside a careful hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只谨慎的手旁有一株绿芽。

abstract.en: Picture two people meeting again after years.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人多年后再次相见。

examples.en: They cultivate vegetables behind the house.
examples.cn: 他们在屋后种菜。

examples.en: She cultivated the habit of walking at dawn.
examples.cn: 她养成了天亮散步的习惯。

examples.en: Good leaders cultivate the people around them.
examples.cn: 好的领导者培养身边的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cultivate 记成「照料」：cult 是耕种，反复照料，土地和本事都会长。

root: 源自拉丁语 cultivare（耕作），更早出自 colere（耕种、敬奉）；本义是翻土种地，后引申为培养能力、习惯与人际关系。

sensesIntro.en: From working the soil, to growing a skill, to tending a friendship.
sensesIntro.cn: 从整治土地，到培养本事，再到经营友谊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand loosening soil around a young shoot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在新苗周围松土。

branches.en: Land must be broken and planted before it feeds anyone.
branches.cn: 土地要先翻开放种，才能养活人。

branches.en: A skill is watered in small amounts every day.
branches.cn: 本事靠每天一点点的浇灌。

branches.en: Friendship is a plant that needs regular care.
branches.cn: 友谊是一株需要常常照料的植物。

branches.en: Soil and mind answer the same kind of care.
branches.cn: 土地与心智回应同一种照料。

branches.en: Habits and friendships both die when neglected.
branches.cn: 习惯与友谊一旦荒废都会死去。

intro.en: Cultivate belongs to the Latin colere family, which also gives culture and agriculture.
intro.cn: cultivate 属于拉丁语 colere 一族，culture 与 agriculture 也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin colere, to till and to honour, is the root under cultivation and culture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 colere（耕种、敬奉）是 cultivation 与 culture 背后的根。

items.meaning: the act of tilling or developing
a person or machine that tills
items.example: The cultivator broke the hard soil.
Uncultivated land lay beyond the fence.

items.meaning: the way a people lives and thinks
items.meaningCN: 一个族群的生存与思维方式
items.exampleCN: 文化塑造我们打招呼的方式。

items.meaning: of a people's way of life
items.example: The city has a rich cultural life.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市文化生活丰富。

definition_zh: 耕种；栽培；（微生物的）培养；修养；培养（能力、关系）
definition_en: the act of tilling land, growing crops or organisms, or developing a quality, person or relationship through sustained care
core_image: 一块被反复翻土、除草、浇水的田，土面松软，作物按行生长，田边放着种子袋与记录本
scene: 田垄被翻得松软，农人蹲下检查幼苗的根系，远处水渠正缓缓放水。Careful cultivation keeps the seed bed open to air and water.
sceneCN: 这里指「对土地反复翻耕与照管」（第 1 个义项：耕作土地）；句意为细致的耕作让苗床保持通气与水分。

pos.zh: 耕种；栽培；（微生物）培养；修养（多作不可数名词）

derivatives.zh: cultivate + -able（能……的）→ 可耕种的；可培养的
cultivate + -or（施动者或工具）→ 耕作的人；中耕机
cultivate + -ar（名词后缀，二十世纪园艺用语）→ 栽培品种（语义偏移：从动作转为被栽培的品系）
cultivate + -ed（过去分词作形容词）→ 耕作的；有教养的
un-（否定）+ cultivated → 未开垦的；未受教育的
re-（重新）+ cultivate → 重新耕作（语义偏移：荒废之后再翻种）

senses.title: Break and tend the soil
senses.definition: to prepare land by ploughing, digging and weeding so that crops can grow
senses.definitionCN: 通过犁翻、挖掘与除草备好土地，使作物得以生长
senses.example: Cultivation of the heavy clay begins in early spring.
senses.exampleCN: 对这种重黏土的耕作从早春开始。
senses.why: The Latin root colere meant to till and to dwell on land, so the first sense is simply the farmer's work on the soil.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 colere 本义是耕作、居住于土地，因此第一义就是农人对土壤的劳作。

senses.title: Growing a named crop
senses.definition: the raising of a particular crop on prepared land, as in rice cultivation
senses.definitionCN: 在备好的土地上种植特定作物，如水稻种植
senses.example: Rice cultivation requires level fields and steady water.
senses.exampleCN: 水稻种植需要平整的田块与稳定的水。
senses.why: Once land is prepared, the same word names the crop put into it, because the whole cycle counts as one practice.
senses.whyCN: 土地备好之后，同一个词就指种进去的作物，因为整个周期算作一项实践。

senses.title: Raising garden plants or trees
senses.definition: the deliberate growing of ornamental plants, fruit trees or forest seedlings
senses.definitionCN: 有意栽培观赏植物、果树或林木幼苗
senses.example: The cultivation of olives spread along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 橄榄的栽培沿海岸传播开来。
senses.why: The verb extended from field crops to any plant that people tend rather than gather wild.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词从田里的作物扩展到任何由人照管、而非野外采集的植物。

senses.title: Growing microorganisms in a medium
senses.titleCN: 在培养基中培养微生物
senses.definition: the controlled growth of bacteria, cells or tissue in a prepared medium
senses.definitionCN: 在配好的培养基中受控地培养细菌、细胞或组织
senses.example: Cultivation of the sample revealed two distinct bacterial colonies.
senses.exampleCN: 对样本的培养显示出两种不同的菌落。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century microbiology borrowed the agricultural word because a culture dish is a small field where organisms are fed and grown.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的微生物学借用了农业词，因为培养皿就是一块喂养、培育生物的小田。

senses.title: Developing a skill or habit
senses.definition: the gradual development of an ability, habit or quality through repeated practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复练习逐步发展某种能力、习惯或品质
senses.example: Cultivation of patience takes longer than learning the rules.
senses.exampleCN: 培养耐心比学会规则要花更长时间。
senses.why: Growing a plant and growing a habit share one shape: small repeated acts of care produce a result that cannot be rushed.
senses.whyCN: 种植植物与培养习惯形状相同：反复的小小照料产生无法催快的结果。

senses.title: Keeping a relationship or contact
senses.definition: the deliberate effort to maintain a friendship, contact or useful connection
senses.definitionCN: 有意维持友谊、联系或有用的关系
senses.example: The diplomat's cultivation of local leaders lasted years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位外交官对当地领袖的经营持续多年。
senses.why: A relationship, like a crop, needs regular attention; neglect is the weed that takes it over.
senses.whyCN: 关系如同作物，需要定期照料；疏忽就是接管它的杂草。

senses.title: Refinement of mind and manners
senses.definition: the refined state of a person's mind, taste or manners, produced by education and good company
senses.definitionCN: 由教育与良好交往造就的心智、趣味或举止上的修养
senses.example: Her cultivation showed in the way she listened before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她的修养体现在先听完再回答的方式上。
senses.why: The metaphor turns inward: what is tilled is no longer soil but the person, and the harvest is poise rather than grain.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转向内部：被耕的不再是土壤而是人，收获的也不是谷物而是从容。

senses.title: Guiding a person's growth
senses.definition: the work of developing someone's abilities and character under sustained guidance
senses.definitionCN: 在持续指导下发展某人的能力与品格
senses.example: The older musician's cultivation of young players saved the ensemble.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年长音乐家对年轻乐手的培养拯救了整个乐团。
senses.why: The agricultural image completes itself: a gardener who tends seedlings is a mentor who tends beginners.
senses.whyCN: 农业意象在此闭合：照看幼苗的园丁，就是照看初学者的师长。

intro.en: Cultivation comes from Latin cultura, a tilling or care, built on cultus, the past participle of colere, to till, inhabit or worship. The noun reached English through Middle French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultivation 来自拉丁 cultura「耕作、照料」，其基础是 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」的过去分词 cultus。这个名词经中古法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Colere meant to till the soil, to dwell on land and to honour a god; Roman usage treated these as one act of tending. Its deeper root is generally connected with a verb meaning to turn or move around, but that link is a reconstruction.
items.cn: colere 意为耕作土地、居住于土地、敬奉神明；罗马用法把这三者视为同一种照料。它更深的词根一般认为与表示「转动、绕行」的动词有关，但这一联系属重构形式。

items.en: The past participle cultus described land that had been worked and a life that had been ordered; it also named care and worship.
items.cn: 过去分词 cultus 描述被耕作过的土地与被整理过的人生，也指照料与敬奉。

items.en: Cultura named the act of tilling and the care given to a field, a body or a mind; it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: cultura 指耕作的行为，以及对田地、身体或心智的照料；它是这个英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Middle French cultivation carried the learned noun into English in the fifteenth century, first in agricultural and religious writing.
items.cn: 中古法语 cultivation 在十五世纪把这个学术名词带入英语，最初用于农业与宗教文本。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century the word was used for growing microorganisms in a prepared medium, a sense borrowed from the image of a small cultivated field.
items.cn: 从十九世纪后期起，这个词用于在配好的培养基中培养微生物，这一义借自「一小块被耕作的田」的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-Latin origin of colere is reconstructed rather than attested, and the earliest English use is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：colere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，并非有据可查；英语最早用例的年代也只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root that name neighbouring things; group two holds verbs and nouns for the work of raising plants.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词根、指相邻事物的词；第二组是表示「培育植物」这项工作本身的动词与名词。

entries.definition: From the same Latin cultura but naming the whole way of life, arts and beliefs of a group, not the act of tilling.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁 cultura，却指一个群体的生活方式、艺术与信念整体，而非耕作行为。

entries.definition: From Latin cultus, it names a religious system or a devoted following, preserving the worship sense that agriculture dropped.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cultus，指宗教体系或狂热的追随群体，保留了农业义所丢弃的「敬奉」义。

entries.definition: Latin ager, field, plus cultura: the science and business of farming, broader than the care of one plot.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 ager「田地」加 cultura：农业的科学与产业，比单块土地的耕作更广。

entries.definition: Latin hortus, garden, plus cultura: the art of growing garden plants, narrower than cultivation in general.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 hortus「园子」加 cultura：栽培园艺植物的技艺，比泛指的 cultivation 更窄。

entries.definition: The mechanical working of soil, such as ploughing and harrowing; it stops at the soil and does not cover crops, microbes or manners.
entries.definitionCN: 对土壤的机械作业，如犁耕与耙地；只到土壤为止，不涵盖作物、微生物或举止。

entries.definition: The whole business of raising crops and animals; cultivation is one part of it, the care of soil and plants.
entries.definitionCN: 种植作物与饲养动物的整个产业；cultivation 只是其中一部分，即对土壤与植物的照料。

entries.definition: Care given to something while it grows, especially a child or a talent; it stresses the caring relationship rather than the technique.
entries.definitionCN: 对生长中之物的照料，尤指孩子或才能；强调照料关系而非技术。

entries.definition: The controlled reproduction of plants or animals to select desired traits; cultivation grows them, breeding chooses the stock.
entries.definitionCN: 为选育理想性状而控制植物或动物的繁殖；cultivation 负责栽培，breeding 负责选种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: colere 'to till' plus -ation 'the act': the act of tilling, and then of tending anything else.
normal.cn: colere「耕作」加 -ation「行为」：耕作的行为，随后扩展到照管别的东西。

normal.en: The family runs cultivate, cultivation, cultivator, cultivable, cultivar, cultivated.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cultivate、cultivation、cultivator、cultivable、cultivar、cultivated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: rice cultivation, shifting cultivation, intensive cultivation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出田间义：水稻种植、轮歇耕作、集约耕作。

normal.en: Laboratory use keeps the field image: a culture dish is a small plot for microbes.
normal.cn: 实验室用法保留田地意象：培养皿就是给微生物的一小块地。

normal.en: The inward sense appears in the fixed phrase cultivation of the mind.
normal.cn: 内向义出现在固定搭配「心性修养」中。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every shelf is a row of seedlings and the reader is the farmer.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每一排书架都是一行幼苗，读者就是农夫。

abstract.en: Picture a friendship watered once a week, never flooded and never left dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一段每周浇一次水的关系，既不被淹没，也不被晒干。

abstract.en: Picture a violin teacher adjusting a beginner's hand as a gardener ties a young tree to a stake.
abstract.cn: 想象小提琴老师调整初学者的手，如同园丁把小树绑在支柱上。

examples.en: Terrace cultivation holds the soil on slopes that would otherwise wash away.
examples.cn: 梯田耕作保住了那些本来会被冲走的山坡土壤。

examples.en: The cultivation of bacteria requires sterile tools and a controlled temperature.
examples.cn: 培养细菌需要无菌器具与受控温度。

examples.en: His cultivation of the committee's trust made the reform possible.
examples.cn: 他对委员会信任的经营使改革成为可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: cult（耕种、培育）+ -ivation（行为）→ 反复照管让东西长起来；土地、细菌、才能、关系都能被培育，名词就是这一过程。

root: 拉丁 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」→ cultus「耕过的、受照料的」→ cultura「耕作、培育」→ 中世纪拉丁 cultivatio；colere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: soil is broken, a crop is tended, and the same tending is then applied to microbes, skills, contacts, manners and a pupil.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先翻土，再照管作物，随后把同一种照管用于微生物、技能、人脉、举止与学生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field is broken, sown and weeded until the soil, the crop and finally the farmer's own mind are all under care.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块田被翻、被种、被除草，直到土壤、作物以及农夫自己的心智都处在照料之下。

branches.en: THE FIELD CYCLE: preparing ground and putting a named crop into it.
branches.cn: 田间周期：先备好地，再把某一种作物种进去。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: the same care applied to plants that are not field crops.
branches.cn: 园圃：把同一种照料用于并非田间作物的植物。

branches.en: THE DISH: a laboratory medium is a small field for invisible organisms.
branches.cn: 培养皿：培养基就是给看不见的生物的一小块田。

branches.en: REPEATED CARE: habits and friendships both grow by regular, unhurried attention.
branches.cn: 反复照料：习惯与友谊都靠规律而不急躁的关注生长。

branches.en: THE INWARD HARVEST: manners and pupils are the last crops, ripened by the same patience.
branches.cn: 内在的收获：举止与学生是最后的作物，由同一种耐心催熟。

intro.en: Cultivation is a Latin noun built from a verb root and a suffix, and both parts also build a large English family, so the word can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: cultivation 是由动词词根与后缀构成的拉丁名词，这两部分还构成一个庞大的英语词族，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin colere supplies cultus, cultura and cultivare; the suffix -ation turns a verb of tending into the name of the work or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 colere 衍生出 cultus、cultura 与 cultivare；后缀 -ation 把表示照管的动词变成工作或其结果的名称。

items.meaning: to till; to dwell; to worship
items.example: The root names the whole act of tending land.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名照料土地的全部动作。

items.example: The participle became a noun for care and worship.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词转为表示照料与敬奉的名词。

items.example: Cultura is the direct ancestor of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: cultura 是这个英语名词的直接祖先。

items.example: Medieval Latin built a new verb from the old participle.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语从旧分词造出一个新动词。

items.meaning: the work of tilling or tending
items.example: The noun names the work and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指工作及其结果。

items.example: The suffix also builds preservation and navigation.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀还构成 preservation 与 navigation。

items.structure: cultivate + -or (one who acts or a tool)
items.meaning: a person or machine that tills
items.example: The cultivator loosened the rows between the vines.
items.exampleCN: 中耕机松开了藤行之间的土。

items.meaning: able to be tilled or grown
items.example: Only the valley floor is cultivable.
The cultivated slope held its soil.
items.exampleCN: 这块被耕作的坡地保住了土壤。

definition_en: relating to the way of life, art, and beliefs of a group of people
core_image: 一条老街上，戏台、书店和庙挤在同一条巷子里
scene: 老街上戏台、书店和庙挤在一条巷子里，都是这座城的样子。The festival is the cultural heart of the town.
sceneCN: 这里 cultural 指「文化的」（第 1 个义项：与一个群体的生活方式、艺术和信仰有关）；句意是这个节庆是这座镇的文化核心。

senses.title: Of a way of life
senses.definition: relating to the customs and beliefs of a group
senses.definitionCN: 与一个群体的习俗和信仰有关的
senses.example: Food is a cultural matter, not just a physical one.
senses.exampleCN: 饮食是文化问题，不只是生理问题。
senses.why: What a group repeats becomes its way of life.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体反复做的事，就成了它的生活方式。

senses.title: Of art and learning
senses.definition: relating to art, music, books, and learning
senses.definitionCN: 与艺术、音乐、书籍和学问有关的
senses.example: The city offers many cultural events.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市有很多文艺活动。
senses.why: A society keeps its best made things on show.
senses.whyCN: 一个社会把做得最好的东西摆出来给人看。

senses.title: Of refined taste
senses.definition: showing refined taste and education
senses.definitionCN: 表现出修养与教育的
senses.example: She moves in cultural circles.
senses.exampleCN: 她出入有文化气息的圈子。
senses.why: Training of the mind leaves a visible mark.
senses.whyCN: 心智受过训练，会留下看得见的痕迹。

intro.en: Cultural is Latin cultura, tilling, plus -alis, belonging to; English formed it in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: cultural 由拉丁语 cultura（耕种）加 -alis（属于）构成，十九世纪在英语中成形。

items.en: Cultura meant tilling the soil and giving care.
items.cn: cultura 指耕种土地并加以照料。

items.en: -Alis meant belonging to or relating to.
items.cn: -alis 意为属于或关于。

items.en: Cultural first meant of cultivation, of land or mind.
items.cn: cultural 最初指耕种或心智培养的。

items.en: It shifted to the arts and way of life of a people.
items.cn: 它转向一个群体的艺术与生活方式。

items.en: It now covers food, dress, music, and belief.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖饮食、服饰、音乐与信仰。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cult- stem, and the meaning group names other words for social life and taste.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cult- 词干，近义组列出其他关于社会生活与品味的说法。

entries.definition: the way of life of a people
trained and refined
a small group with strong beliefs
of art and its making
of people living together
polished in manner and taste
entries.definitionCN: 举止与品味经过打磨的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a narrow street holding a stage and a temple and end with a trained eye.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一条挤着戏台与庙的窄巷开始，落到一双受过训练的眼睛。

normal.en: Culture plus -al makes an adjective about a whole way of life.
normal.cn: culture 加 -al，成了描述整套生活方式的形容词。

normal.en: A festival can be the heart of a town.
normal.cn: 一个节庆可以是一座镇的心脏。

normal.en: Cultural things are learned from others, not carried in blood.
normal.cn: 文化的东西是向别人学来的，不写在血里。

normal.en: Food, dress, and songs all carry culture.
normal.cn: 饮食、服饰与歌都带着文化。

normal.en: A cultured person shows what a culture trained.
normal.cn: 有修养的人，显出文化训练过的痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a stage lit beside a small bookshop.
abstract.cn: 想象一座亮着灯的戏台挨着小小书店。

abstract.en: Picture hands passing food across a long table.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手把食物递过长桌。

abstract.en: Picture a child copying a dance step.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子跟着学舞步。

examples.en: The two countries began a cultural exchange.
examples.cn: 两国开始了文化交流。

examples.en: Old songs are part of our cultural heritage.
examples.cn: 老歌是我们文化遗产的一部分。

examples.en: The town has a busy cultural life.
examples.cn: 这镇的文化生活很热闹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cultural 记成「种出来的」：culture 原是耕种，一个群体长期养出的习惯与艺术，就是文化。

root: 由拉丁语 cultura（耕种、照料）加形容词后缀 -alis 构成；十九世纪进入英语，本义与栽培有关，后指一个群体的艺术、信仰与生活方式。

sensesIntro.en: From a group's way of life, to its arts, to a refined manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个群体的生活方式，到它的艺术，再到文雅的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stage, a bookshop, and a temple in one narrow street.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条窄巷里同时有戏台、书店和庙。

branches.en: Customs shared by a group are called cultural.
branches.cn: 一个群体共享的习俗被称为文化的。

branches.en: Art and learning are the visible face of that life.
branches.cn: 艺术与学问是这种生活看得见的脸。

branches.en: A trained taste shows culture in one person.
branches.cn: 受过训练的品味，把文化显在一个人身上。

branches.en: A way of life and its art cannot be separated.
branches.cn: 生活方式与它的艺术分不开。

branches.en: What a society makes, a person can learn to love.
branches.cn: 社会做出来的东西，个人可以学着去爱。

intro.en: Cultural sits in the Latin cultura family, with culture, cultured, and agriculture around it.
intro.cn: cultural 属于拉丁语 cultura 一族，周围有 culture、cultured 与 agriculture。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cultura, tilling, is the root that carries -al into cultural.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cultura（耕种）是把 -al 带进 cultural 的根。

items.exampleCN: 从文化上说，这两座镇不同。
伦敦是座多元文化城市。
社会与文化的力量塑造品味。

definition_en: increasing by successive additions, or resulting from a total built up over time
core_image: 沙漏下方的沙堆一层层加高
scene: 这组词中，The cumulative effect of small emissions became visible after a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 cumulative 是「累积的」（第 2 个义项：多次小影响累加成的总效应）；句意：微小排放的累积效应十年后才显现出来。图中可辨识物件：沙漏、逐年排放柱状图、上升曲线、工厂烟囱、十年刻度。

pos.zh: 累积的；渐增的；累计的（常作定语）

senses.title: Growing by successive additions
senses.titleCN: 逐次累加的：一层压一层地增长
senses.definition: increasing as each new amount is added to what already exists
senses.definitionCN: 随着每一新量加到既有数量上而增长
senses.example: The cumulative growth of the archive surprised the librarians.
senses.exampleCN: 档案的累积增长让馆员们感到意外。
senses.why: Latin cumulare means 'to heap up', from cumulus 'heap'. The adjective describes anything built by adding layer upon layer rather than by one jump.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 cumulare 意为“堆起”，来自 cumulus“堆”。这个形容词描述任何靠一层层添加、而非一步跳升而形成的事物。

senses.title: The total effect of many small causes
senses.titleCN: 累积效应：小事重复造成的总后果
senses.definition: describing an effect produced by repeated small causes acting over time
senses.definitionCN: 指由重复的小原因长期作用所产生的效应
senses.example: The cumulative effect of small emissions became visible after a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 微小排放的累积效应十年后才显现出来。
senses.why: A single small cause may be harmless, but heaping them together crosses a threshold, so the adjective names the total rather than any one item.
senses.whyCN: 单个小原因也许无害，但把它们堆起来就会越过某个阈值，因此这个形容词命名的是总体，而非任何单项。

senses.title: A running total in statistics
senses.titleCN: 累计数：统计里一路加下去的和
senses.definition: in statistics, describing a total formed by adding each value in turn
senses.definitionCN: 统计中把每个数值依次相加形成的总数
senses.example: The cumulative frequency column reaches one hundred per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 累积频数列最终达到百分之百。
senses.why: The statistical sense makes the heap exact: each row adds one more item to the pile, and the column shows the pile at every step.
senses.whyCN: 统计义把“堆”精确化：每一行往堆上再加一项，整列显示每一步的堆积高度。

senses.title: Cumulative evidence in law
senses.titleCN: 累积证据：多条单独不足、合起来有力
senses.definition: in law, describing separate pieces of evidence that strengthen one another when taken together
senses.definitionCN: 法律中指多条证据合在一起时互相增强
senses.example: The court admitted the records as cumulative evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院将这些记录作为累积证据采纳。
senses.why: Each item adds weight rather than replacing the others; the legal sense treats proof as a heap that grows heavier with every piece.
senses.whyCN: 每一项都在增加分量，而非替代其他项；法律义把证明看成一堆越加越重的东西。

senses.title: Cumulative interest or dividend
senses.titleCN: 累积利息／股息：未付部分滚存
senses.definition: in finance, describing interest or dividends that accumulate and must be paid later
senses.definitionCN: 金融中指利息或股息累积起来、须在以后支付
senses.example: The preferred shares carry cumulative dividends.
senses.exampleCN: 这些优先股带累积股息。
senses.why: Money that is not paid now is heaped onto the next payment, so the finance sense is the literal heap transferred from sand to unpaid amounts.
senses.whyCN: 现在未付的钱被堆到下一次支付上，因此金融义就是把沙堆的字面意象转移到未付金额。

senses.title: Lifetime accumulated risk
senses.titleCN: 累积风险：一生中反复暴露的总账
senses.definition: in medicine and public health, describing risk that adds up over repeated or prolonged exposure
senses.definitionCN: 医学与公共卫生中指重复或长期暴露累加起来的风险
senses.example: Cumulative exposure to sunlight raises the risk of skin damage.
senses.exampleCN: 长期累积的日晒会增加皮肤损伤风险。
senses.why: Risk is measured over a lifetime, not a single day: each exposure adds a small amount to the total, so the adjective marks the sum rather than the episode.
senses.whyCN: 风险按一生而非单日衡量：每次暴露都在总量上加一点，因此形容词标记的是总和，而非单次事件。

senses.title: Accumulated damage in materials
senses.titleCN: 累积损伤：材料一次次受载后的总损耗
senses.definition: in engineering, describing damage that builds up through repeated stress
senses.definitionCN: 工程中指反复受力逐步积累的损伤
senses.example: Engineers track cumulative damage in the turbine blades.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师追踪涡轮叶片的累积损伤。
senses.why: Materials do not fail from one load but from many; the adjective names the damage that has been heaped up beyond the visible single event.
senses.whyCN: 材料不是因一次载荷失效，而是因多次载荷失效；这个形容词命名的正是超出单次可见事件的堆积损伤。

senses.title: Cumulative culture
senses.titleCN: 累积文化：一代代叠加改进
senses.definition: in anthropology, describing knowledge or technology that improves through repeated additions across generations
senses.definitionCN: 人类学中指知识或技术经代际反复添补而改进
senses.example: Cumulative culture allows each generation to start from earlier tools.
senses.exampleCN: 累积文化让每一代人都从更早的工具出发。
senses.why: Culture is a heap that never resets: each generation adds a small improvement and passes the larger pile on, which is why human technology can outrun individual invention.
senses.whyCN: 文化是一堆不会清零的东西：每代添一点改进，再把更大的堆传下去，这正是人类技术能超越个人发明的原因。

intro.en: Cumulative is cumul- + -ive, from Latin cumulare 'to heap up'. The same stem gives accumulate and the cloud name cumulus, both built on the image of a pile.
intro.cn: cumulative 是 cumul- + -ive，来自拉丁 cumulare“堆起”。同一词干还产生 accumulate 与云名 cumulus，二者都建立在“堆”的意象上。

items.en: cumulus meant 'a heap, mass or pile'. It was used of piled earth or grain and later gave the meteorological term for heaped clouds.
items.cn: cumulus 意为“堆、堆块”。它曾用于堆起的土或谷物，后来产生指堆状云的气象术语。

items.en: cumulare 'to heap up, amass' was formed from cumulus. Its past participle cumulatus supplies the stem cumulat- used in English.
items.cn: cumulare“堆起、积聚”由 cumulus 构成。其过去分词 cumulatus 提供英语使用的词干 cumulat-。

items.en: The suffix -ive, from Latin -ivus 'having the nature of', makes an adjective of tendency: cumulative describes what tends to heap up or what results from heaping.
items.cn: 后缀 -ive 来自拉丁 -ivus“具有……性质的”，构成表倾向的形容词：cumulative 描述倾向于堆积的事物，或由堆积产生的结果。

items.en: English cumulative appears in the 17th century, first in learned and legal writing about totals and evidence. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 cumulative 于17世纪出现，最早见于讨论总数与证据的学术和法律文本。年代为约数。

items.en: Statistics, finance, medicine and engineering each adopted the word for their own running totals in the 19th and 20th centuries.
items.cn: 统计学、金融、医学与工程分别在19、20世纪采用这个词来表示各自的累计总量。

items.en: The deeper origin of Latin cumulus is uncertain; it is often treated as a derivative of a root meaning 'heap', but no single reconstruction is agreed. Exact English dates are approximate.
items.cn: 拉丁 cumulus 的更深来源不确定；常被视为某个意为“堆”的词根的派生，但没有公认的单一重构。英语确切年代为约数。

note.en: The first group contains look-alike words from different roots; the second contains words for totals and growth that count differently.
note.cn: 第一组是来自不同词根的形近词；第二组是计算方式不同的“总量／增长”类词。

entries.definition: Tending to accumulate; it stresses the habit or process of collecting, while cumulative usually describes the resulting total.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于积累的；强调收集的习惯或过程，而 cumulative 通常描述形成的总量。

entries.definition: A heap-shaped cloud; the noun names the pile itself, not the process of adding to it.
entries.definitionCN: 积云；这个名词命名堆本身，而非堆积过程。

entries.definition: Relating to a climax or highest point, from Latin culmen 'top'. It looks like cumulative but has no heap in it.
entries.definitionCN: 与顶点、高潮有关的，来自拉丁 culmen“顶”。它形似 cumulative，但词源里没有“堆”。

entries.definition: Already gathered into a store; it describes the completed stock, while cumulative describes the adding process or its pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 已经聚集起来的；描述完成的存量，而 cumulative 描述添加过程或其模式。

entries.definition: A total formed by combining separate items; it does not imply growth over time.
entries.definitionCN: 由各项合并而成的总数；不暗示随时间增长。

entries.definition: Increasing by small steps; it stresses the size of each step, while cumulative stresses the total reached.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步小幅增加的；强调每步的幅度，而 cumulative 强调达到的总量。

entries.definition: Shared by or belonging to a group; it is about ownership or joint action, not heaping over time.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体共享或属于群体的；关乎归属或共同行动，而非长期堆积。

entries.definition: Continuing step by step over time; it can describe growth but not necessarily a total.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间逐步持续的；可描述增长，但不必形成总量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphology, fixed collocations and the genuine cumulus family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁构词、固定搭配与真实的 cumulus 词族。

normal.en: cumulus 'heap' + -ive: the adjective describes whatever is formed by heaping.
normal.cn: cumulus“堆”+ -ive：这个形容词描述一切靠堆积形成的东西。

normal.en: accumulate and cumulative share the same heap, one as a verb and one as an adjective.
normal.cn: accumulate 与 cumulative 共享同一个“堆”，一个是动词，一个是形容词。

normal.en: Learn cumulative effect, cumulative total and cumulative evidence; these are the three most common academic uses.
normal.cn: 记住 cumulative effect、cumulative total、cumulative evidence；这是三个最常见的学术用法。

normal.en: cumulus clouds are heaps of cloud, which is the same picture as a cumulative total.
normal.cn: cumulus 云就是堆状的云，与累计总数的画面相同。

normal.en: Do not confuse cumulative with culminative: one heaps, the other reaches a top.
normal.cn: 不要把 cumulative 与 culminative 混淆：一个是堆，一个是到达顶点。

abstract.en: Picture sand falling through an hourglass, each grain adding to one growing cone.
abstract.cn: 想象沙粒穿过沙漏，每一粒都加到一个不断长高的圆锥上。

abstract.en: Picture a wall built one brick per day until it is thick enough to change the weather behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象每天只砌一块砖的墙，直到厚到足以改变墙后的天气。

abstract.en: Picture an interest ledger where unpaid amounts roll into the next row and grow larger each time.
abstract.cn: 想象一本利息账簿，未付金额滚入下一行，每次都变得更大。

examples.en: The cumulative total of donations passed one million dollars.
examples.cn: 捐款累计总额超过了一百万美元。

examples.en: Repeated small delays had a cumulative effect on the schedule.
examples.cn: 反复的小延误对进度产生了累积效应。

examples.en: The report assesses the cumulative impact of tourism on the coast.
examples.cn: 报告评估了旅游业对海岸的累积影响。

dict_mnemonic.text: “Q（cu）mulate（堆）”——像 Q 一样一圈圈堆上去 → cumulative 累积的、渐增的

root: 拉丁 cumulus“堆、堆块”→ cumulare“堆起、积聚”→ cumulat- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one image: a heap that grows by addition. The heap may be sand, data, evidence, unpaid interest, exposure, damage or cultural knowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个意象：靠添加而增高的堆。这堆东西可以是沙、数据、证据、未付利息、暴露量、损伤或文化知识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cone of sand growing grain by grain.
core.cn: 核心意象：沙粒逐颗落下、不断长高的圆锥。

branches.en: ADDING: successive growth and a statistical running total are the same addition seen qualitatively and numerically.
branches.cn: 添加：逐次增长与统计累计数，是同一加法在性质与数量两个层面的呈现。

branches.en: THRESHOLD DAMAGE: small causes and repeated stress both become serious only after the heap is large enough.
branches.cn: 阈值损伤：小原因与反复应力，都要等堆足够大才变得严重。

branches.en: LAW AND FINANCE: separate evidence and unpaid dividends both add weight or value without replacing the earlier items.
branches.cn: 法律与金融：分散证据与未付股息都在增加分量或价值，而不取代先前项目。

branches.en: LIFETIME EXPOSURE: risk adds up across many episodes, so the total matters more than any single exposure.
branches.cn: 终生暴露：风险在多次事件中累加，因此总量比任何单次暴露更重要。

branches.en: CULTURE: improvements accumulate across generations, making the heap inherited rather than personal.
branches.cn: 文化：改进在代际间累积，使这堆东西成为继承物而非个人成就。

intro.en: Cumulative is a Latin adjective in -ive built on the participle stem cumulat-. The related verb accumulate adds the prefix ad- to the same base.
intro.cn: cumulative 是建立在分词词干 cumulat- 上的拉丁 -ive 形容词。相关动词 accumulate 在同一词基上加前缀 ad-。

latinIntro.en: Latin cumulus 'heap' gives cumulare 'to heap up' and the adjective cumulativus. English borrowed the stem as cumulat- and added -ive, while accumulate came through the prefixed form accumulare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cumulus“堆”产生 cumulare“堆起”与形容词 cumulativus。英语借入词干 cumulat- 并加 -ive，而 accumulate 经带前缀形式 accumulare 进入。

items.meaning: tending to heap up; formed by accumulation
items.meaningCN: 累积的；渐增的（cumulat- + -ive 表倾向）
items.example: The cumulative effect was larger than expected.

items.exampleCN: 灰尘在架子上积了起来。

items.meaning: a mass that has been gathered
items.meaningCN: 积累物；堆积（-ion 结果名词）
items.example: The accumulation of sediment blocked the channel.
items.exampleCN: 沉积物堆积堵塞了水道。

items.meaning: by adding one item to another
items.meaningCN: 累积地；渐增地（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: Cumulatively, the changes altered the whole system.
items.exampleCN: 这些变化累积起来改变了整个系统。

items.example: Cumulus clouds formed above the hills.

items.meaning: a device that stores energy or data
items.meaningCN: 蓄电池；累加器（-or 表装置）
items.example: The accumulator stores charge between cycles.
items.exampleCN: 蓄电池在循环之间储存电荷。

items.meaning: a running count of values up to a point
items.meaningCN: 累积频数（逐项累加的计数）
items.example: The cumulative frequency rises steadily across the table.
items.exampleCN: 累积频数在整张表中稳步上升。

items.meaning: separate proofs that reinforce one another
items.example: The judge described the letters as cumulative evidence.
items.exampleCN: 法官把这些信件称为累积证据。

items.meaning: tending to collect or pile up
items.meaningCN: 倾向于积累的（-ive 表倾向）
items.example: The accumulative habit of note-taking paid off.
items.exampleCN: 做笔记的积累习惯最终有了回报。

definition_zh: adj. 有疗效的；n. 治疗物
definition_en: able to cure or heal
core_image: 一碗苦药下肚，疼处慢慢松开
scene: 这种草药据说有疗效。The herb is said to have a curative effect.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：curative 指有疗效的；句意是这种草药据说有疗效。

senses.title: Healing
senses.definition: able to make a sick person well
senses.definitionCN: 能使病人康复
senses.example: The plant has curative properties.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物有治疗功效。
senses.why: A bitter drink loosening a pain.
senses.whyCN: 一碗苦药松开疼痛。

senses.title: Restoring health
senses.definition: helping the body return to health
senses.definitionCN: 帮助身体恢复健康
senses.example: Rest is curative after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 手术后休息有助康复。
senses.why: A body warming back to strength.
senses.whyCN: 身体慢慢回暖有力。

senses.title: A remedy
senses.definition: a substance or treatment that cures
senses.definitionCN: 能治病的药物或疗法
senses.example: They sold a folk curative.
senses.exampleCN: 他们卖一种民间药。
senses.why: A jar of dark herbs.
senses.whyCN: 一罐深色草药。

intro.en: Curative comes from Latin curare, to care for or heal, plus the suffix -ive.
intro.cn: curative 源自拉丁语 curare（照料、治愈），加后缀 -ive 构成。

items.en: Cura meant care.
items.cn: cura 意为照料。

items.en: Curare meant to care for or heal.
items.cn: curare 意为照料、治愈。

items.en: Curativus meant fitted for healing.
items.cn: curativus 意为适于治疗的。

items.en: Curative described healing power.
items.cn: 十五世纪 curative 形容治疗功效。

items.en: Curative opposed preventive medicine.
items.cn: 十九世纪 curative 与预防医学相对。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cur- stem; the near-meaning group names healing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cur- 词干；近义组都是治愈。

entries.definition: To make a sick person well.
Wanting to learn more.
A person who looks after a collection.
Able to make someone healthy.
Intended to cure a problem.
Relating to the treatment of illness.
Bringing back strength.

normalIntro.en: Curative is care strong enough to make you well.
normalIntro.cn: curative 就是强到能把人治好的照料。

normal.en: Cura means care.
normal.cn: cura 意为照料。

normal.en: Curare means to heal.
normal.cn: curare 意为治愈。

normal.en: The suffix -ive means tending to.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ive 意为有…倾向。

normal.en: So curative means tending to heal.
normal.cn: 因此 curative 意为有疗效的。

normal.en: A curative herb eases an illness.
normal.cn: 有疗效的草药能缓解疾病。

abstract.en: A bitter drink loosening a pain.
abstract.cn: 一碗苦药松开疼痛。

abstract.en: A body warming back to strength.
abstract.cn: 身体慢慢回暖有力。

abstract.en: A jar of dark herbs.
abstract.cn: 一罐深色草药。

examples.en: The treatment had a curative effect.
examples.cn: 这种治疗有疗效。

examples.en: Some herbs are curative, not preventive.
examples.cn: 有些草药是治疗性的，而非预防性的。

examples.en: They tested the curative powers of the plant.
examples.cn: 他们测试了这种植物的治疗功效。

dict_mnemonic.text: cura（照料）+ -ative（有…作用的）→ 有疗效的。

root: 拉丁 cura（照料）→ curare（治愈）→ curativus → 英语 curative

sensesIntro.en: Care powerful enough to bring health back.
sensesIntro.cn: 强到能把健康带回来的照料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bitter drink easing a pain away
core.cn: 核心意象：一碗苦药让疼痛慢慢松开

branches.en: A bitter drink loosening a pain.
branches.cn: 一碗苦药松开疼痛。

branches.en: A body warming back to strength.
branches.cn: 身体慢慢回暖有力。

branches.en: A jar of dark herbs.
branches.cn: 一罐深色草药。

branches.en: Cure that continues into recovery.
branches.cn: 延续到康复的治疗。

branches.en: A remedy that rebuilds strength.
branches.cn: 重建体力的药。

intro.en: Curative is Latin curare plus -ive, from cura, care.
intro.cn: curative 由拉丁语 curare 加 -ive 构成，源于 cura（照料）。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura means care, and curare means to heal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 意为照料，curare 意为治愈。

definition_en: to keep something under control, or the raised stone edge of a road
core_image: 一只手拉紧缰绳，让跑得太快的马慢下来
scene: 骑手拉紧缰绳，让跑得太快的马慢下来。The city hopes to curb the rise in traffic.
sceneCN: 这里 curb 指「抑制、控制」（第 1 个义项：让某事不再增长或加剧）；句意是这座城市希望抑制交通量的增长。

senses.title: Hold something back
senses.definition: to keep something from growing or getting worse
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某事增长或恶化
senses.example: New rules curb the use of plastic bags.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定限制塑料袋的使用。
senses.why: A strong force needs a bit to hold it.
senses.whyCN: 强大的力量需要一点东西勒住。

senses.title: The edge of a road
senses.definition: the raised stone edge along a road
senses.definitionCN: 路边凸起的石边
senses.example: She parked the car at the curb.
senses.exampleCN: 她把车停在路边。
senses.why: A low stone line keeps wheels off the grass.
senses.whyCN: 一条矮石线，把车轮挡在草外。

senses.title: A check or limit
senses.definition: a limit placed on something
senses.definitionCN: 加在某事上的限制
senses.example: The government put a curb on spending.
senses.exampleCN: 政府对开支设了限制。
senses.why: A curb is a line you are not meant to cross.
senses.whyCN: 路缘是一条不该越过的线。

intro.en: Curb comes from Old French courbe, curved, from Latin curvus, bent; a curb bit was a curved piece of metal for a horse.
intro.cn: curb 源自古法语 courbe（弯曲之物），更早出自拉丁语 curvus（弯的）；勒马的马衔就是一块弯金属。

items.en: Curvus meant bent or curved.
items.cn: curvus 意为弯曲的。

items.en: Courbe named something curved.
items.cn: courbe 指弯曲之物。

items.en: Curb first meant a curved bit for a horse.
items.cn: curb 最初指勒马的弯形马衔。

items.en: It came to mean a check or restraint.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示制止与约束。

items.en: It also named the stone edge of a street.
items.cn: 它也指街道边凸起的石缘。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cur- opening, and the meaning group names other ways of holding something back.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cur- 开头，近义组列出其他拉住某物的说法。

entries.definition: a solid with six square faces
a curved piece of hair
to make a sick person well
to hold someone back from acting
entries.definitionCN: 拉住某人使其不作某事

entries.definition: to keep something below a level
entries.definitionCN: 使某事不超过某一水平

entries.definition: the outer line of a surface

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a pulled rein and end with a low stone line beside a road.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被拉紧的缰绳开始，落到路边一条矮石线。

normal.en: A curb bit sits in a horse's mouth and asks it to slow.
normal.cn: 马衔放在马嘴里，请它慢下来。

normal.en: To curb a thing is to put a bit on it.
normal.cn: curb 一件事，就是给它套上嚼子。

normal.en: Curb the temper before it becomes a shout.
normal.cn: 在脾气变成喊声前先勒住它。

normal.en: The curb keeps cars off the grass.
normal.cn: 路缘把车挡在草地外。

normal.en: Every fast thing needs a small edge to stop it.
normal.cn: 每个太快的东西，都需要一道小边来挡住。

abstract.en: Picture a horse slowing as the reins go tight.
abstract.cn: 想象缰绳一紧，马就慢下来。

abstract.en: Picture a shoe stepping off a stone edge into the road.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鞋从石边踩下马路。

abstract.en: Picture a red line on a chart flattening out.
abstract.cn: 想象图上一根红线渐渐变平。

examples.en: The new tax is meant to curb waste.
examples.cn: 这项新税意在抑制浪费。

examples.en: He curbed his anger and spoke softly.
examples.cn: 他压住怒火，轻声说话。

examples.en: A bicycle lay against the curb.
examples.cn: 一辆自行车靠在路缘上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 curb 记成「勒住」：马的弯曲嚼子勒住速度，就是抑制。

root: 源自古法语 courbe（弯曲之物），更早出自拉丁语 curvus（弯的）；本义是勒马的弯曲嚼子，后引申为约束与路缘。

sensesIntro.en: From pulling a horse back, to limiting a force, to a stone edge beside the road.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把马勒住，到限制一股力量，再到路边的石缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pulling a rein to slow a horse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拉紧缰绳让马慢下来。

branches.en: A check keeps a strong force from running away.
branches.cn: 约束让强大的力量不至于失控。

branches.en: The stone edge is a curb for wheels.
branches.cn: 石缘是给车轮设的路缘。

branches.en: A limit is a line drawn and kept.
branches.cn: 限制是一条画下并守住的线。

branches.en: To curb and to set a curb are the same act.
branches.cn: 抑制与设限是同一个动作。

branches.en: A road edge shows how a limit looks in stone.
branches.cn: 路缘把限制的样子用石头做出来。

intro.en: Curb forms words for restraining, for the horse bit, and for the stone edge of a street.
intro.cn: curb 组成一族词，关于抑制、马衔与街道石缘。

latinIntro.en: The Latin curvus, bent, is the root behind curb and its compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 curvus（弯的）是 curb 及其合成词背后的根。

items.meaning: the stone edge of a road
the side of a road near the edge
a bit that controls a horse
items.example: The rider used a curb bit.

items.meaning: the weight of a car without load
how attractive a house looks from the street

items.exampleCN: 没有路缘的街道让车慢下来。

definition_en: a strong wish to know or learn, or a strange and interesting thing
core_image: 一个孩子蹲在地上，盯着一只翻身的甲虫看很久
scene: 孩子蹲在地上，盯着一只翻身的甲虫看了很久。Her curiosity made her open every drawer in the house.
sceneCN: 这里 curiosity 指「好奇心」（第 1 个义项：强烈想知道或学习的愿望）；句意是好奇心让她把家里每个抽屉都打开了。

senses.title: Wish to know
senses.definition: a strong wish to know or learn something
senses.definitionCN: 强烈想知道或了解某事的愿望
senses.example: Curiosity led her to ask questions all day.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心让她整天问问题。
senses.why: A mind that wants an answer will not sit still.
senses.whyCN: 想要答案的心，坐不住。

senses.title: A strange object
senses.definition: an object that is strange and interesting
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪而有趣的东西
senses.example: The shop sells old maps and curiosities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖旧地图和稀奇玩意儿。
senses.why: Things that do not fit the pattern get kept.
senses.whyCN: 不合常规的东西，会被留下来。

senses.title: Interest in others' affairs
senses.definition: an eagerness to know about other people's private lives
senses.definitionCN: 急于知道别人私事的愿望
senses.example: Her curiosity about the neighbours annoyed them.
senses.exampleCN: 她对邻居的好奇让他们不快。
senses.why: Not every question is welcome.
senses.whyCN: 并不是每个问题都受欢迎。

intro.en: Curiosity comes from Latin curiositas, the wish to know, from cura, care.
intro.cn: curiosity 源自拉丁语 curiositas（求知的愿望），其根是 cura（关心）。

items.en: Cura meant care and attention.
items.cn: cura 意为关心与用心。

items.en: Curiosus meant careful, then eager to know.
items.cn: curiosus 意为用心的，后来指急于知道。

items.en: Curiositas named the wish to learn.
items.cn: curiositas 指求知的愿望。

items.en: Curiosite kept the wish to know.
items.cn: curiosite 保留了求知的愿望。

items.en: Curiosity also named a rare object worth keeping.
items.cn: curiosity 也指值得收藏的稀奇物件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cur- stem, and the meaning group names other kinds of interest in knowing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cur- 词干，近义组列出其他想了解的说法。

entries.definition: wanting to know something
in a curious way
to make a sick person well
a wish to know more about something
entries.definitionCN: 想更多了解某事的愿望

entries.definition: a feeling of surprise and question
a habit of asking many questions

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a child and a beetle and end with a drawer pulled open.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从孩子与甲虫开始，落到被拉开的抽屉。

normal.en: Curiosity is care that will not let a question go.
normal.cn: 好奇心是不肯放过问题的关心。

normal.en: A child can watch one beetle for an hour.
normal.cn: 一个孩子能盯着一只甲虫看一小时。

normal.en: Every drawer in the house was opened once.
normal.cn: 家里每个抽屉都被打开过一次。

normal.en: The same word keeps old maps in a shop.
normal.cn: 同一个词也收着店里的旧地图。

normal.en: Curiosity about neighbours is often not welcome.
normal.cn: 对邻居的好奇，常常不受欢迎。

abstract.en: Picture a small face very close to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一张贴得很近地面的小脸。

abstract.en: Picture a finger lifting a stone to see what lives under it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指掀起石头，看下面住着什么。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of odd things with paper labels.
abstract.cn: 想象一架贴着纸标签的稀奇物件。

examples.en: Curiosity made him read the whole letter.
examples.cn: 好奇心让他读完了整封信。

examples.en: She asked, out of pure curiosity, where he had been.
examples.cn: 她纯粹出于好奇，问他去了哪里。

examples.en: The old shop is full of curiosities.
examples.cn: 这家老店满是稀奇玩意儿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 curiosity 记成「关心到非弄明白不可」：拉丁语 cura 是关心，往前一步就是好奇。

root: 源自拉丁语 curiositas（求知的愿望），其根是 cura（关心）；本义是用心探究，后指好奇心，也指因稀奇而被收藏的物件。

sensesIntro.en: From a wish to know, to a strange object, to interest in other people's lives.
sensesIntro.cn: 从想知道的愿望，到稀奇物件，再到对别人生活的兴趣。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child crouching over a beetle, unwilling to leave.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个孩子蹲在甲虫旁，舍不得走。

branches.en: A mind that needs the answer keeps asking.
branches.cn: 非要答案的心，会一直问下去。

branches.en: An odd object is kept because it raises questions.
branches.cn: 稀奇物件被留下，是因为它引出问题。

branches.en: The same pull can turn toward other people.
branches.cn: 同一股拉力，也会转向别人的生活。

branches.en: The wish to know and the odd thing feed each other.
branches.cn: 想知道的愿望与稀奇物件互相喂养。

branches.en: A collector and a gossip both follow curiosity.
branches.cn: 收藏者与爱打听的人，都跟着好奇心走。

intro.en: Curiosity belongs to the Latin cura family, with curious and cure close by.
intro.cn: curiosity 属于拉丁语 cura 一族，curious 与 cure 都在旁边。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cura, care, is the root that turned into curiosity and curious.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura（关心）是变成 curiosity 与 curious 的根。

items.example: The child is curious about ants.
She looked curiously at the box.
items.exampleCN: 她好奇地看着那只箱子。

items.example: He was incurious about the world.

items.meaning: a shop selling odd old things
items.example: They found it in a curiosity shop.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一家旧货店找到它。

items.example: The museum began as a cabinet of curiosities.
items.exampleCN: 这座博物馆最初是一只珍奇柜。
